stories.headline: Navy picks Boeing for F/A-XX sixth-gen fighter in $20B+ deal, beating Northrop Grumman

key_facts.fact: On September 29, 2026, the US Navy selected Boeing to build its sixth-generation carrier-based strike fighter, F/A-XX, beating Northrop Grumman.
key_facts.excerpt: Boeing has been selected to build the Navy's sixth-generation carrier-based strike fighter, dubbed F/A-XX, icing out what was considered to be its biggest competitor in late-stage negotiations, Northrop Grumman.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon valued the agreement at more than $20 billion for the full-scale development phase, procuring multiple test aircraft; the jet is to fly for the Navy beginning in the 2030s.
key_facts.excerpt: Per a Pentagon release ... the agreement is "valued at more than $20B for the full-scale development phase. The contract procures multiple test aircraft for ground, airworthiness, systems, and weapons integration testing." The statement added that the F/A-XX will fly "beginning in the 2030s" for the Navy.

key_facts.fact: The win makes Boeing the sole US supplier of sixth-generation fighters, after it won the Air Force's F-47 program in March 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The selection locks Boeing in as the sole supplier of sixth-generation fighters for the US. In March 2025, Boeing won the right to develop and produce the Air Force's next-gen fighter, dubbed the F-47.

key_facts.fact: F/A-XX is intended to replace the Navy's F/A-18 Super Hornet fleet; Boeing said technical and programmatic details remain classified.
key_facts.excerpt: F/A-XX is intended to replace the service's fleet of F/A-18 Super Hornets. ... The technical and programmatic details of F/A-XX remain classified under U.S. national security and export laws.

key_facts.fact: Under Secretary of Defense Michael Duffey called F/A-XX a 'crucial, non-negotiable investment' in US air combat capability.
key_facts.excerpt: "The F/A-XX platform represents a crucial, non-negotiable investment in America's national security and long-term air combat capabilities," Michael Duffey, under secretary of defense for acquisition and sustainment, stated.

key_facts.fact: The program had been subject to years of funding disputes, with engineering and supply-chain concerns prompting some Pentagon officials to push for delay.
key_facts.excerpt: The F/A-XX program ... has been the subject of funding disputes for years, with engineering and supply chain concerns prompting some Pentagon officials to push for delaying the program.

stories.headline: Russia opens winter campaign with mass strike on Ukraine's grid; NATO scrambles jets

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian PM Serhii Koretskyi said the overnight attack into September 30 was Russia's first mass combined strike on Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the end of the previous heating season.
key_facts.excerpt: "Since the summer, there has effectively not been a single day when the enemy did not attack energy infrastructure. But such a massive and combined attack took place for the first time since the end of the previous heating season," he said.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 188 drones, 86 of them jet-powered, plus ballistic and cruise missiles; five missiles and 155 drones were downed, with impacts at 18 locations.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's air force said that Russia launched 188 drones -- 86 of which were jet-powered -- and an unspecified number of ballistic and cruise missiles ... five missiles and 155 drones were destroyed or neutralized, with impacts reported across 18 locations.

key_facts.fact: The strikes killed seven people, including a child, and wounded 24, according to AP.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian missiles and drones killed seven people, including a child, and wounded 24 in a major overnight barrage that struck civilian areas and Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Centrenergo said the attack damaged generating equipment at the Trypilska thermal power plant in the Kyiv region.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's attack damaged generating equipment at the Trypilska Thermal Power Plant in the Kyiv region, state-owned energy company Centrenergo said.

key_facts.fact: Poland scrambled military aircraft and Romania scrambled two Spanish F-18s in response to the strikes on western Ukraine; a drone exploded in Moldova, damaging a communications antenna.
key_facts.excerpt: NATO military aircraft were scrambled in both Poland and Romania overnight ... Two Spanish F-18 jets were scrambled "to monitor the situation" ... a drone exploded and damaged a communications antenna in the Anenii Noi district

key_facts.fact: NATO on Tuesday denounced Russia's 'irresponsible nuclear rhetoric' after Russia's embassy in Belgium said Moscow was ready to use its entire arsenal if NATO tried to blockade Kaliningrad.
key_facts.excerpt: "We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric. We call on Russia to end its unprovoked war in Ukraine," a NATO spokesperson said

key_facts.fact: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers on September 29 urged Trump not to ease Russia sanctions after reports he backs trading sanctions relief for the release of political prisoners.
key_facts.excerpt: A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers urged President Donald Trump on Sept. 29 not to ease sanctions against Russia, amid reports that his administration is considering sanctions relief in exchange for the release of political prisoners.

stories.headline: US sends Iran feedback on seven-day Hormuz ceasefire plan via Qatar as Treasury adds sanctions

key_facts.fact: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi received US feedback via Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday (Sept 29) on Iran's seven-day trust-building plan; sequencing is the main sticking point.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi received US feedback via Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday on a seven-day plan aimed at building trust between Washington and Tehran, with sequencing the main sticking point

key_facts.fact: The plan outlines a seven-day period aimed at returning both sides to an enhanced version of the June memorandum of understanding, including concrete steps on Iran's nuclear program.
key_facts.excerpt: The document being circulated outlines a seven-day period of trust-building aimed at returning the two sides to an enhanced version of the memorandum of understanding agreed in June, including concrete steps on Iran's nuclear programme

key_facts.fact: Araghchi briefed Iran's Cabinet on the US proposal on Wednesday; Iran's earlier offer sought sanctions relief, a ceasefire and the unfreezing of $12 billion in assets in exchange for gradually lifting its Hormuz blockade.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran had put forward a peace proposal last week that would have gradually lifted its blockade over the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief, a ceasefire and the unfreezing of $12 billion in assets.

key_facts.fact: The US Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and entities, including some in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan, accused of procuring weapons and components for Iran's MODAFL.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Treasury Department sanctioned 10 individuals and entities in multiple jurisdictions that it said procured weapons and weapons components for Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL).

key_facts.fact: IRGC spokesperson Gen. Hossein Mohebbi said the war will end only if Washington admits defeat and published a 'letter to the American people' urging protests against Trump ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms.
key_facts.excerpt: A spokesperson for Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guard Corps, Gen. Hossein Mohebbi, said Tuesday the only way the war with the U.S. will end is if Washington admits defeat and leaves.

key_facts.fact: Trump claimed the US had taken more oil out of the Strait of Hormuz in recent days than at any point in history and said Tehran was 'doing very poorly'.
key_facts.excerpt: "You know, we took more oil out of the Hormuz Strait over the last couple of days than at any point in history," Trump told reporters at the White House.

stories.headline: US core PCE inflation slows to 3.0%, below forecasts, a day after confidence hit a 12-year low

key_facts.fact: The PCE price index rose 0.3% in August and 3.4% year over year; core PCE rose 0.2% on the month and 3.0% annually, BEA reported on September 30.
key_facts.excerpt: From the same month one year ago, the PCE price index for August increased 3.4 percent. Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 3.0 percent from one year ago.

key_facts.fact: Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had expected 3.7% headline and 3.3% core annual PCE; BEA changed methodology for software, portfolio management fees and legal services, with unclear impact.
key_facts.excerpt: Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had been looking for increases of 0.3% and 3.7% respectively. ... The respective forecasts were for 0.3% and 3.3%.

key_facts.fact: Consumer spending surged 0.9% in August after a downwardly revised 0.1% gain in July.
key_facts.excerpt: Consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of economic activity, surged 0.9% last month after a downwardly revised 0.1% gain in July, the BEA said.

key_facts.fact: On September 29 the Conference Board consumer confidence index fell to 81.9 from 88.6, a 12-year low, and August JOLTS job openings fell to a 5-month low.
key_facts.excerpt: Weaker-than-expected US economic news also weighed on stocks after Aug JOLTS job openings fell to a 5-month low, and Sep consumer confidence tumbled to a 12-year low.

key_facts.fact: The 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.6206% on September 29, highest since June 2002, and the 10-year reached 5.293%, highest since June 2007.
key_facts.excerpt: the 30-year bond hitting 5.6206 per cent, its highest since June 2002. The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury bond climbed to 5.293 per cent – its highest level since June 2007.

key_facts.fact: New York Fed President John Williams said he saw no urgency to hike again, cutting market odds of an October hike to about 51.5% from nearly 70%; odds were 47.1% after the PCE data.
key_facts.excerpt: Traders are pricing in a 47.1 percent chance of the FOMC hiking rates by a quarter point in late October, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

key_facts.fact: WTI crude fell $3.22 to settle at $89.38 on September 29 as the US Energy Department offered up to 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
key_facts.excerpt: WTI (X6) SETTLED USD 3.22 LOWER AT 89.38/BBL ... US DoE offers up to 40mln barrels from SPR.

stories.headline: MI5 tells UK universities to cut ties with Chinese institute it calls a spy-agency front

key_facts.fact: On September 30, 2026, MI5 issued a Security Service Espionage Alert saying the primary purpose of the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) is to fund research improving the Ministry of State Security's espionage capability.
key_facts.excerpt: On 30 September 2026, MI5 issued a Security Service Espionage Alert stating that the primary purpose of the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) ... is to fund research that directly improves Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS) technical capability for espionage.

key_facts.fact: More than 100 UK-linked academics have contributed to MSS-funded projects via CGTRI, some without knowing the funding source.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 100 UK-linked academics have contributed to research projects funded by MSS via CGTRI. In some cases, academics may not be aware that CGTRI is funding the Chinese research project they are contributing to.

key_facts.fact: Projects covered AI, cybersecurity, covert communications systems and steganography.
key_facts.excerpt: UK academics have contributed to CGTRI-funded projects on topics including Artificial Intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, covert communications systems and steganography.

key_facts.fact: It is the first time MI5 has independently issued a public alert of this kind about a research institute serving as an arm of Chinese state intelligence.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, the security service has taken the unusual step of independently issuing a public alert to warn about a research institute that serves as an arm of Chinese state intelligence.

key_facts.fact: Security Minister Dan Jarvis wrote to every UK university vice-chancellor to end all arrangements with CGTRI, warning continued collaboration could breach the National Security Act 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: He said he had written to university chiefs "to ensure they support their staff to end all arrangements with this company," adding that collaborating with the research institute could breach the National Security Act.

key_facts.fact: The Guardian noted the alert risks casting a shadow over UK-China cooperation at a time when the bilateral relationship is enjoying a revival.
key_facts.excerpt: risks casting a shadow over UK-China cooperation at a time when the bilateral relationship is enjoying a revival.

stories.headline: Robinhood unveils 24/7 weekend stock trading, crypto perpetual futures and earnings contracts

key_facts.fact: At its HOOD Summit in Houston on September 29, Robinhood announced 24/7 weekend trading for select US equities, pending regulatory review, powered by alternative trading system Bruce ATS.
key_facts.excerpt: Coming soon, pending regulatory review, Robinhood is expanding its trading hours to let customers trade a selection of U.S. equities 24/7, including weekends. ... Weekend trading is powered by Bruce ATS

key_facts.fact: It is the first time Robinhood will allow weekend trading; its 24 Hour Market, launched in 2023, runs Sunday 8pm to Friday 8pm ET and at times accounts for up to 25% of daily volume on busy days.
key_facts.excerpt: About 10 months after launching the feature, the company said as much as 25% of the total daily ... volume on busy days came from outside traditional hours. This is the first time Robinhood is allowing weekend trading.

key_facts.fact: Eligible US customers will be able to trade crypto perpetual futures on eight assets with up to 10x leverage on bitcoin and ether (3x on others), offered via Bitstamp at one basis point per trade through year-end.
key_facts.excerpt: It also intends to offer up to 10x leverage on bitcoin and ether perpetuals and 3x leverage for other perpetual futures. The company said the perps offering will be supported by Bitstamp and will charge 0.01% per trade through the end of the year.

key_facts.fact: Robinhood also announced earnings contracts, binary options listed through Cboe letting customers trade on company metrics such as EPS and revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also announced earnings contracts, binary options products listed through Cboe that allow customers to trade on company-specific financial metrics such as whether a company beats earnings or hits a revenue target.

key_facts.fact: Both the NYSE and Nasdaq have filed to expand their trading hours, as retail brokerage competition shifts from low costs to access and speed.
key_facts.excerpt: Both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq have filed to expand their trading hours, while Robinhood launched its 24 Hour Market in 2023. That service still stops on weekends.

key_facts.fact: CEO Vlad Tenev said Robinhood is delivering tools once reserved for hedge funds, big banks and quant firms.
key_facts.excerpt: "We're making Robinhood the best place in the world for active traders by delivering tools once reserved for hedge funds, big banks, and quant firms."

stories.headline: South Korea's Kospi ends Q3 as world's worst major market, down about 19% on chip-stock unwind

key_facts.fact: The Kospi closed the quarter on September 30 at 6,838.04, down 19.33% for the quarter, its largest one-quarter decline since Q1 2020, snapping a six-quarter winning streak (Dow Jones Market Data).
key_facts.excerpt: The KOSPI Composite Index is down 1638.44 points or 19.33% this quarter to 6838.04 --Largest one-quarter percentage decline since the 1st quarter 2020 --Snaps a six-quarter winning streak

key_facts.fact: The index is still up 62.26% year to date and sits 24.98% below its record close of 9,114.55 on June 22, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: --Off 24.98% from its record close of 9114.55 hit Monday, June 22, 2026 ... --Year-to-date it is up 2623.87 points or 62.26%

key_facts.fact: Kospi was the weakest major index globally in Q3, versus China's CSI 300 down 12.5% and the S&P 500 up 2.3%.
key_facts.excerpt: Kospi plunges 18.8% in Q3, underperforming all major equity indices as AI-linked trades unwind, compared to China's CSI 300 falling 12.5% and S&P 500 rising 2.3%.

key_facts.fact: The decline was driven by a memory-chip sell-off that began in July as the year's most popular AI trades were liquidated.
key_facts.excerpt: It fell 18.8% over the three months, dragged down by a sell-off in memory-chip stocks that began in July as the year's most popular AI trades were liquidated.

key_facts.fact: The FT, as reported by Donga Ilbo, tied the July rout partly to the unwinding of hedge fund Situational Awareness's heavily leveraged positions in Korean memory stocks; the Bank of Korea has also shifted to tightening.
